Month in brief

Retirement notice: MDE and XDR Advanced Hunting APIs retiring; migrate to Microsoft Graph Security API leads 2303 Defender updates

January 2026 recorded 27 new, 2239 updated, 27 removed Microsoft Defender documentation changes and 10 relevant Message Center announcements. The most active areas were Endpoint, Defender XDR, Identity.

  • Defender XDR · Hunting and detection
    Retirement notice: MDE and XDR Advanced Hunting APIs retiring; migrate to Microsoft Graph Security API

    Microsoft is retiring the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs by February 1, 2027. Organizations must manually migrate workflows to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027, to ensure continued functionality and improved security integration.

  • Vulnerability Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure
    Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management and Microsoft Security Exposure Management integration

    Added Microsoft Defender documentation in defender-vulnerability-management/microsoft-defender-vulnerability-management-exposure-management.md.

  • Exposure Management · Vulnerabilities and exposure
    Predefined classifications - Microsoft Security Research

    Updated Microsoft Defender documentation in exposure-management/predefined-classification-rules-and-levels.md.

  • Endpoint · Incidents and response
    Use Microsoft Defender for Endpoint sensitivity labels to protect your data and prioritize security incident response

    Updated Microsoft Defender documentation in defender-endpoint/information-protection-investigation.md.

  • Identity · Identity protection
    Microsoft Defender for Identity XDR security alerts

    Updated Microsoft Defender documentation in defender-for-identity/alerts-xdr.md.

For Defender administrators

Review the linked Microsoft Learn changes that apply to your managed platforms, policies, applications, and rollout plans. The archive preserves the source diff for verification.

Microsoft Teams: Report a suspicious call

New

Microsoft Teams will introduce a "Report a Call" feature by mid-March 2026, allowing users to flag suspicious one-to-one calls. Reports share limited call metadata with organizations and Microsoft, viewable in Microsoft Defender portal or Teams Admin Center. The feature is enabled by default but can be disabled by admins.

Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Admins can block external users in Microsoft Teams from Defender Portal

New

Starting mid-February 2026, admins can block external Microsoft Teams users via the Tenant Allow/Block List in the Microsoft Defender portal, controlling access and deleting existing communications. This applies to Teams and Defender XDR, with audit logging and limits of 4,000 domains and 200 emails blocked.

New Built-in Alert Tuning Rules optimize your incident and alert queues

New

Starting January 25, 2026, Microsoft Defender XDR introduces built-in alert tuning rules focusing on low-severity Office 365 alerts, with automated triage and reopening if needed. Active from February 5, these rules help SOCs prioritize alerts, with an opt-out window until February 5 and multi-tenant management support.
